root_cause.text: The pcrypt AEAD wrapper in `crypto/pcrypt.c` mishandled asynchronous crypto return codes by treating only `-EINPROGRESS` as an in-flight request, so `-EBUSY` from `MAY_BACKLOG` requests was incorrectly processed as a completed error and its `complete` callback path was not filtered properly.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `|| ret == -EBUSY` to both `pcrypt_aead_enc()` and `pcrypt_aead_dec()`, and adds `if (err == -EINPROGRESS) return;` in `pcrypt_aead_done()`, matching the commit message “MAY_BACKLOG requests can return EBUSY” and “filtering out EINPROGRESS notifications.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Ignore -EINPROGRESS completion callbacks in pcrypt_aead_done so only final AEAD results are processed.
intent_record.what: In pcrypt_aead_done(), two lines were added at the start of the function: an if-statement that checks whether err equals -EINPROGRESS and immediately returns when it does.
intent_record.how: This prevents the rest of the completion handler from running for in-progress notifications, so only real completion outcomes are recorded into padata->info and passed to padata_do_serial().

intent_record.intent_summary: Treat `-EBUSY` as an asynchronous encryption in-progress state to avoid incorrectly handling it as a failure.
intent_record.what: The conditional after `crypto_aead_encrypt(req)` was changed from checking only `ret == -EINPROGRESS` to checking `ret == -EINPROGRESS || ret == -EBUSY` before returning.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now treats `-EBUSY` the same way as an in-progress asynchronous encryption request, so it returns immediately instead of storing the error in `padata->info`. This prevents `-EBUSY` from being misinterpreted as a completed failure and allows the async encryption path to continue behaving correctly when the crypto backend reports temporary resource exhaustion.

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle `-EBUSY` from AEAD decryption as an asynchronous in-progress result to avoid premature failure handling.
intent_record.what: In `pcrypt_aead_dec`, the conditional return now checks for both `-EINPROGRESS` and `-EBUSY` instead of only `-EINPROGRESS` after calling `crypto_aead_decrypt(req)`.
intent_record.how: This changes the function to treat a `-EBUSY` return from the AEAD decrypt operation the same way as an in-progress asynchronous request, allowing the callback path to defer completion instead of incorrectly recording the error immediately.

candidates.rationale: This condition only treats -EINPROGRESS as an in-flight async request. Under MAY_BACKLOG, crypto_aead_encrypt() can return -EBUSY for a pending async operation, but this check falls through and incorrectly handles it as a completed error.

This condition only filters -EINPROGRESS as asynchronous progress. When crypto_aead_decrypt() returns -EBUSY for backlog/asynchronous processing, the code mistakenly continues into error handling instead of treating it as in-flight.

Because the completion callback did not properly exclude -EBUSY/in-flight cases, this assignment records the return value as a final result and feeds it into the serial completion path, causing premature error processing.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition only recognizes -EINPROGRESS as an in-flight async AEAD operation. Under MAY_BACKLOG, crypto_aead_encrypt()/crypto_aead_decrypt() can return -EBUSY for pending asynchronous work, so failing to treat -EBUSY here causes the code to drop into error/completion handling prematurely.

When the return value is -EBUSY, storing it directly into padata->info records a backlog/in-progress request as a final result. That feeds the completion path with an error status instead of deferring until the async operation actually completes.

The completion callback records the status into padata->info without properly excluding backlog/in-flight cases. This propagates the premature error handling triggered by misclassifying -EBUSY as a completed failure.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function bodies already contain the fix described by the commit. In both `pcrypt_aead_enc()` and `pcrypt_aead_dec()`, the crypto call result is stored in a local `ret` first (`ret = crypto_aead_encrypt(req);` / `ret = crypto_aead_decrypt(req);`), and only `ret == -EINPROGRESS` is treated as in-flight (`if (ret == -EINPROGRESS) return;`). Crucially, `padata->info = ret;` is assigned only after that check, which avoids overwriting the return code before the async path completes. This means the vulnerable construct (writing `padata->info` immediately from the crypto return and relying only on `-EINPROGRESS`) is not present here.
